learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Applied knowledge of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Knowledge and capacities for the application of environmental materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: Technologies for urban and industrial wastewater treatment
Physico-chemical techniques for contaminated soil treatment
Presentations of practical cases and reports on environmental management and technologies
teaching_methods: Introductory activities (course presentation and description of practical activities)
Laboratory practices (experimentation on pollutant determination and wastewater treatment)
Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) workshop (computer lab practice with Simapro software, problem-solving, report delivery)
Presentations of individual or small group works (analysis of practical cases of management and emerging treatment technologies, oral presentations and subsequent debate)
Thematic seminar (introduction to waste management and treatment, video viewing)
Thematic seminar (gamification-based educational activity on Genially platform for solving technical problems in a wastewater treatment plant)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participatory attitude in practical activities
Practical test on seminars and laboratory practices
Elaboration and presentation of practical case and debate

assessment_rules: To pass the course, the score obtained in the theoretical exam must be 4 or higher. If this minimum value is not met, the score obtained from practical activities will not count towards the final grade, which will then correspond to the theoretical exam grade. Spelling correction will be valued in written tests, and spelling errors may reduce the corresponding score. An alternative evaluation system, consisting of an 80% written test and a 20% practical case presentation with a prior report, may be requested by students only in exceptional cases as contemplated by the University of Jaén's Academic and Student Evaluation Regulations.
